name: Vidhana Soudha
description: Karnataka’s neo-Dravidian legislature building is a defining Bengaluru landmark, best viewed from the public approaches around Cubbon Park.
how_to_reach: Reach central Bengaluru by Metro, bus, taxi or auto-rickshaw; the nearest Metro stations are Cubbon Park and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Vidhana Soudha.
practical_notes: The legislature is not a walk-in tourist monument. Observe security restrictions and use designated public viewpoints. Seasonal lighting and access arrangements vary.
entry_fee: Public exterior viewing; access restrictions apply

name: Mysuru Palace
description: The former royal palace of Mysuru combines Indo-Saracenic architecture, ceremonial halls and an important place in the city’s Dasara traditions.
how_to_reach: Located in central Mysuru, reachable by city bus, taxi or auto-rickshaw from Mysuru Junction and the airport.
practical_notes: Ticketing, illuminated-evening displays and holiday hours vary. Confirm current visitor rules with Karnataka Tourism before travel.
entry_fee: Check current palace ticket rates

name: Badami Cave Temples
description: Rock-cut cave temples carved into red sandstone cliffs above Agastya Lake, representing early Chalukyan art and architecture.
how_to_reach: Badami is reached by road and rail from Hubballi, Bengaluru and Vijayapura; local vehicles connect the station and cave complex.
practical_notes: October to March is generally more comfortable. Monument timings and entry charges should be confirmed before visiting.
entry_fee: ASI ticket rates apply

name: Hampi Group of Monuments
description: A UNESCO World Heritage landscape of Vijayanagara-era temples, markets, tanks and boulder-strewn hills around the Tungabhadra River.
how_to_reach: Hospet is the main rail and road gateway; continue by taxi, bus, bicycle or authorised local transport to Hampi.
practical_notes: Allow multiple days for the spread-out sites. Protected-monument ticketing, electric vehicle rules and heat conditions vary by season.
entry_fee: Selected protected monuments require tickets

name: Gokarna and Om Beach
description: Gokarna combines a pilgrimage town with a series of Arabian Sea coves, including the distinctive crescent-shaped Om Beach.
how_to_reach: Reach Gokarna by Konkan Railway, coastal highway buses or taxi from Goa, Hubballi or Mangaluru.
practical_notes: Beach conditions change during the monsoon. Swim only where local safety guidance permits and respect temple customs in town.
entry_fee: Free public beach access

name: Bandipur Tiger Reserve
description: A Project Tiger reserve and national park in the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, comprising dry-deciduous and moist-deciduous forest. Part of the Nilgiri landscape shared with Nagarhole, Mudumalai and Wayanad reserves, it supports tigers, elephants, leopards, gaur and wild dogs.
how_to_reach: Located on the Mysuru–Ooty (Gundlupet) highway, about 80 km from Mysuru and 220 km from Bengaluru. Use authorised forest department entry points; the highway through the reserve is closed from 9 PM to 6 AM.
practical_notes: Safari permits, buffer-zone and core-zone access, timings and seasonal closures are controlled by the forest department. Book jeep safaris through the official online portal or at the gate. Wildlife sightings are never guaranteed.
entry_fee: Forest safari and entry charges apply; separate fees for Indian nationals and foreign visitors
address: Bandipur, Gundlupet taluk, Chamarajanagar district, Karnataka

name: Nandi Hills
description: A hilltop getaway north of Bengaluru known for cooler mornings, viewpoints and historic hill-station remains.
how_to_reach: Reach by road from Bengaluru or Chikkaballapura; pre-dawn trips require checking current gate and vehicle rules.
practical_notes: Weekend sunrise visits can be crowded. Confirm entry hours, parking rules and weather conditions before leaving Bengaluru.
entry_fee: Check current entry and parking charges

name: Mullayanagiri Peak
description: Karnataka’s highest peak rises above the coffee country around Chikkamagaluru, with mountain roads, walking routes and broad Western Ghats views.
how_to_reach: Travel by road from Chikkamagaluru town using a local taxi or suitable private vehicle.
practical_notes: Fog, rain and wind can make the route hazardous. Follow local access instructions and avoid off-trail hiking.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking charges may apply

name: Chitradurga Fort
description: A vast hill fort of layered stone walls, gateways, reservoirs and lookout points associated with the Nayakas of Chitradurga.
how_to_reach: Chitradurga is on the Bengaluru–Pune highway and rail corridor; local transport connects the town and fort.
practical_notes: The fort has steep, uneven terrain. Carry water, wear shoes with grip and confirm ASI opening hours.
entry_fee: ASI ticket rates apply

name: St. Mary’s Islands
description: A small offshore island group known for distinctive columnar basalt formations and reached by seasonal boat services from the Udupi coast.
how_to_reach: Take an authorised boat from Malpe; Udupi is connected by rail and road to Mangaluru and Bengaluru.
practical_notes: Boat operations depend on sea conditions and may pause in monsoon. Confirm schedules, life-jacket rules and last-return timings.
entry_fee: Boat and local entry charges apply

name: Murudeshwar Temple and Beach
description: A coastal pilgrimage town centred on the Murudeshwar Shiva temple complex, a large statue and a beach-facing setting.
how_to_reach: Murudeshwar has a railway station on the Konkan line and is accessible by coastal road from Mangaluru, Udupi and Goa.
practical_notes: Temple and tower access rules can change. Dress modestly for worship areas and follow local sea-safety instructions.
entry_fee: Temple entry is generally free; tower access may be charged

name: Jog Falls
description: The Sharavathi River drops through a dramatic gorge at Jog Falls, a seasonal spectacle whose flow and viewpoints vary substantially through the year.
how_to_reach: Reach by road from Shivamogga, Sagara or Honnemardu; the nearest rail and bus links are at Sagara.
practical_notes: Monsoon brings the strongest flow but also wet, slippery conditions. Use marked viewpoints and check local access restrictions.
entry_fee: Check current local entry charges

name: Chennakeshava Temple, Belur
description: A finely detailed Hoysala temple at Belur, recognised with nearby Hoysala monuments as part of the UNESCO World Heritage Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas.
how_to_reach: Belur is reached by road from Hassan, Chikkamagaluru and Mysuru; taxis and buses are available from Hassan.
practical_notes: This is an active temple as well as a protected heritage site. Dress respectfully and confirm photography and ticket rules on arrival.
entry_fee: Check current monument and camera charges

name: Gol Gumbaz
description: The monumental mausoleum of Mohammed Adil Shah is known for its enormous dome and whispering gallery, a landmark of Deccan architecture.
how_to_reach: Vijayapura is served by rail and road from Hubballi, Solapur, Bengaluru and Hyderabad; use local transport from the city centre.
practical_notes: Confirm ASI hours and ticketing. The gallery is reached by steps and can be crowded in peak season.
entry_fee: ASI ticket rates apply

name: Bidar Fort
description: A later-medieval Deccan fort complex with broad ramparts, palace remains and waterworks reflecting Bidar’s Bahmani and Barid Shahi history.
how_to_reach: Bidar is reached by rail and road from Hyderabad, Kalaburagi and Bengaluru; the fort is accessible from town by local transport.
practical_notes: Explore only marked areas and confirm monument opening hours before visiting.
entry_fee: ASI ticket rates apply

name: Dandeli and Kali River
description: Dandeli is a Western Ghats base for forest stays, river-based adventure and regulated access to the Kali landscape.
how_to_reach: Reach Dandeli by road from Hubballi, Goa or Karwar; the nearest railhead is Alnavar, with onward road transport.
practical_notes: Rafting and water activities depend on releases, weather and licensed operators. Verify safety standards, age limits and current availability.
entry_fee: Operator and activity charges vary

name: Coorg Coffee Country
description: The Kodagu highlands around Madikeri are known for coffee estates, forested roads, waterfalls and a distinct regional culture.
how_to_reach: Madikeri is reached by road from Bengaluru, Mysuru and Mangaluru. The nearest major rail link is Mysuru.
practical_notes: Estate visits require permission. Monsoon is scenic but can bring landslides and restricted waterfall access; check local advisories.
entry_fee: Destination and estate charges vary

name: Nagarhole National Park
description: Nagarhole is a major tiger reserve in the Nilgiri Biosphere landscape, visited through regulated safari zones and forest department gates.
how_to_reach: Access is by road from Mysuru, Madikeri or Hunsur; use authorised safari booking channels and designated gates.
practical_notes: Safaris are regulated and sightings cannot be promised. Book through authorised channels and follow forest department instructions.
entry_fee: Forest safari and entry charges apply

name: Sringeri Sharada Peetham
description: A major Advaita monastic centre on the Tunga River, associated with Adi Shankaracharya and centred on the Sharadamba temple.
how_to_reach: Sringeri is reached by road from Chikkamagaluru, Udupi and Shivamogga; local buses and taxis serve the town.
practical_notes: It is an active religious institution. Dress modestly, respect ritual spaces and confirm festival-period access locally.
entry_fee: Free; donations welcome

name: Dharmasthala Manjunatha Temple
description: Dharmasthala is a major pilgrimage town known for the Manjunatha temple, charitable traditions and its multi-faith heritage.
how_to_reach: Reach by road from Mangaluru, Udupi or Bengaluru. Local bus and taxi services connect the temple area.
practical_notes: Follow temple dress and queue rules. Festival dates and special darshan arrangements should be confirmed with official temple channels.
entry_fee: Free general entry; special services vary

name: Pattadakal Group of Monuments
description: A UNESCO World Heritage ensemble of early Chalukyan temples where northern and southern Indian architectural traditions meet along the Malaprabha valley.
how_to_reach: Pattadakal is reached by road from Badami and Bagalkote; Hubballi is a larger transport gateway.
practical_notes: Visit in cooler hours and confirm ASI ticketing. Combine with Badami and Aihole only with enough daylight for travel.
entry_fee: ASI ticket rates apply

name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden
description: A 240-acre botanical garden established by Hyder Ali in 1760 and expanded by Tipu Sultan, featuring a lake, the Victorian-era Glass House modelled on London's Crystal Palace, and a pre-Cambrian granite outcrop with an 18th-century watchtower. One of India's finest botanical collections with over 1,854 species of plants.
how_to_reach: Metro: Lalbagh station (Green Line) is at the east gate. City buses and autos reach all four gates. Nearest railway station: Bengaluru City Junction (4 km).
practical_notes: Open daily 6:00 AM to 7:00 PM. Nominal entry fee applies (check current rates). The Glass House hosts the Republic Day (January) and Independence Day (August) flower shows — these are separately ticketed and very popular. Weekends and flower show periods are crowded; early morning visits are quieter.
entry_fee: Nominal entry fee applies; Glass House flower shows ticketed separately

name: Cubbon Park
description: A 300-acre civic park laid out in 1870 in the centre of Bengaluru, shaded by century-old trees and dotted with public buildings, fountains and memorials.
how_to_reach: Metro: Cubbon Park station. The park is bounded by Kasturba Road, Queen's Road and Dr. Ambedkar Road.
practical_notes: Open daily; some avenues close to vehicles on Sunday mornings.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Bangalore Palace
description: A Tudor-revival palace built in 1878 for the Commissioner of Mysore, purchased in 1884 by Chamaraja Wadiyar X of the Mysore royal family. Set on 33 acres in Vasanth Nagar, it features four towers modelled on Windsor Castle, fortress-like turrets, timber ceilings, tiled lawns and a public gallery. The facade is illuminated on Republic and Independence Days.
how_to_reach: Located on Palace Road, Vasanth Nagar, about 3 km from Bengaluru City Junction. Nearest Metro: Sir M. Visveshwaraya station (Purple Line). Auto-rickshaws readily available from MG Road and Cubbon Park.
practical_notes: Open daily 10:00 AM to 5:30 PM. Ticketed entry applies; audio guides available. The palace may close for private events such as weddings and official functions — confirm availability before visiting. Photography permitted in most areas.
entry_fee: Ticketed entry; rates vary

name: Bannerghatta Biological Park
description: A forest reserve and biological park on the southern edge of Bengaluru known for its butterfly park, lion and tiger safaris and a bear rescue centre on the Mysuru highway corridor.
how_to_reach: About 28 km from Bengaluru city on the Bannerghatta Road; KSRTC buses ply from Kanakapura Road.
practical_notes: Safari quotas and timings are fixed daily; carry photo ID; closed on some holidays.
entry_fee: Park and safari tickets apply

name: ISKCON Temple Bengaluru
description: One of the largest ISKCON centres in India on Hare Krishna Path, with the Radha Krishna shrine, an attached Govinda museum-style dining complex and a library.
how_to_reach: Metro: Mahakavi Kuvempu Road / Rajajinagar; autos from Central Street.
practical_notes: Darshan hours are set around aarti times; the complex is busiest on weekends and Ekadashi.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Devanahalli Fort
description: A moated square fort of mud and stone at Devanahalli, traditional birthplace of Tipu Sultan, whose twin gateways still stand in the old town near the airport.
how_to_reach: About 35 km from Bengaluru on the Airport Road; auto-rickshaws from the bus stand.
practical_notes: The site is not always open beyond the outer walls; photography may be restricted near the gates.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Ghati Subramanya Temple
description: A hillside Karthikeya shrine near Doddaballapura known for its Sarpotsava and Karthika fairs, when thousands of snake-worshippers climb the steps.
how_to_reach: About 35 km from Bengaluru via Doddaballapura; buses and autos from the town.
practical_notes: Steep approach steps, monkeys and heavy festival crowds; avoid peak festival weekends if sensitive to rush.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Makalidurga Hill
description: A boulder-crowned trekking hill north of Bengaluru with a survey tower, a small temple and a reservoir view at dawn.
how_to_reach: About 60 km from Bengaluru via Doddaballapura; hire a taxi for the final village road.
practical_notes: The climb is steep and unprotected in stretches; carry water and start early. Monsoon rocks are slippery.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Avathi Hills
description: A low granite ridge on the Bengaluru Rural–Kolar fringe, known for a small fort shrine and open-rock scrambling.
how_to_reach: Approach from Avathi or Avati Road; no direct public transport to the base.
practical_notes: Unmarked route; go with someone who has done it and confirm local access.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Chamundeshwari Temple, Chamundi Hills
description: The tutelary shrine of the Mysuru royal family on the 1,000 m Chamundi Hills, reached by a rampart road past the famous monolithic Nandi, and central to Dasara rituals.
how_to_reach: 13 km from Mysuru city; taxis and KSRTC buses run up the hill road.
practical_notes: The hill road closes during Dasara processions; steps near the Nandi are crowded on Saturdays.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Mysuru Zoo (Sri Chamarajendra Zoological Gardens)
description: One of India's oldest public zoos, established in 1892 by Krishnaraja Wadiyar IV and laid out in a grove around a lake, known for its gorillas, white tigers, safari zone and century-old trees.
how_to_reach: Located opposite the Mysuru Palace on Mysore-Ooty Road; auto-rickshaw or city bus from all parts of Mysuru.
practical_notes: Open daily except Tuesdays; morning hours typically 8:30 AM to 5:30 PM. Night safari is available on selected evenings and bookable separately. Closed on Republic Day, Independence Day and the day of Dasara procession.
entry_fee: Zoo ticket applies; night safari extra

name: St. Philomena's Church
description: A cruciform neo-Gothic cathedral in Krishnaraja Mohalla with twin 54-metre spires, one of the tallest churches in Asia and a landmark of Mysuru's Catholic community.
how_to_reach: About 3 km from Mysuru Junction; autos and city buses from the fort area.
practical_notes: Service hours restrict sightseeing; photography inside may be limited.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Jaganmohan Palace and Art Gallery
description: A 19th-century Wodeyar palace near Devaraja Market converted into one of Karnataka's oldest public art galleries, holding Mysore-school paintings, sculptures and musical instruments.
how_to_reach: On Dhanvanthi Road, walkable from the fort and Devaraja Market.
practical_notes: Closed weekly; photography policies vary inside.
entry_fee: Museum ticket applies

name: Karanji Lake
description: A lake sanctuary in southern Mysuru with a bird-watching trail, butterfly park and boating, ringed by green space.
how_to_reach: About 5 km from the city centre near the rice museum.
practical_notes: Boating depends on water levels; best birding is early morning.
entry_fee: Lake and boating charges apply

name: Abbey Falls
description: A scenic cascade where the Kannimane and Sujyoti streams join below a coffee-and-spice canopy near Madikeri; flow peaks just after the monsoon.
how_to_reach: About 9 km from Madikeri on the Kushalnagar road; last stretch is a narrow local road.
practical_notes: Beware of leeches in the wet season; viewpoints can be crowded on holidays.
entry_fee: Entry and parking charges apply

name: Raja's Seat, Madikeri
description: A terraced garden on a ridge above Madikeri associated with the erstwhile Coorg kings, famous for sunset views across the Western Ghats.
how_to_reach: Walkable or a short auto ride from Madikeri fort.
practical_notes: Best in clear weather; the garden closes in the evening.
entry_fee: Minor entry charge

name: Talakaveri, Source of the Kaveri
description: The hood-shaped spring source of the River Kaveri in the Brahmagiri hills; the Tula Sankramana festival in mid-October draws lakhs of pilgrims.
how_to_reach: About 8 km from Bhagamandala, 45 km from Madikeri; ghat road, shared jeeps.
practical_notes: Festival weeks mean heavy traffic and queues; tanks are for ritual use, not swimming.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Dubare Elephant Camp
description: A forest-department camp on the Kaveri where rescued elephants are bathed and fed; visitors join timed morning or afternoon interaction sessions.
how_to_reach: About 10 km from Madikeri on the Kushalnagar road; river crossing by boat.
practical_notes: Sessions run on fixed slots and may cancel in high river flow; book in advance.
entry_fee: Elephant interaction charges apply

name: Mandalpatti Viewpoint
description: A grassland-and-shola plateau north of Madikeri ending at the Nalknad rock pillar, reached by a rough jeep track and a short climb.
how_to_reach: About 20 km from Madikeri via Kiggatnal; local jeeps serve the last stretch.
practical_notes: The track is monsoon-sensitive and the summit winds are strong; not suitable for two-wheelers.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Iruppu Falls
description: A twin-step waterfall on the Lakshmana Tirtha in the Brahmagiri forest, a Shiva pilgrimage spot that floods with pilgrims at Shivaratri.
how_to_reach: About 48 km from Madikeri via Somwarpet and the Kutta road.
practical_notes: Forest drive beyond Kutta is unpaved; leeches and spray in monsoon.
entry_fee: Entry and guide charges apply

name: Baba Budangiri Range
description: A sandstone ridge in the Chandragiri forest named for the Sufi pilgrim credited with bringing coffee seeds to India, with cave shrines shared by two faiths.
how_to_reach: About 12 km from Chikkamagaluru town on the Kemmangundi road.
practical_notes: Trek permits and forest timings apply; the ridge closes in heavy rain.
entry_fee: Forest entry applies

name: Hebbe Falls
description: A 178-metre two-tier cascade (Dodda and Chikka Hebbe) below the Kemmangundi ridge in reserved forest.
how_to_reach: Reached by forest jeeps from Kemmangundi after leaving vehicles at the check post.
practical_notes: Jeep quotas are limited in monsoon; the final walk is slippery.
entry_fee: Forest entry, guide and safari charges apply; bookings via forest department channels.

name: Kemmangundi (KR Hills)
description: The former summer resort of the Mysore royal family at about 1,400 m, with the Z Point and Kalhatti Gundu viewpoints above tea and coffee slopes.
how_to_reach: About 30 km from Chikkamagaluru via Baba Budangiri.
practical_notes: Fog can shut the viewpoint; monsoon leeches are common on trails.
entry_fee: Minor entry charges

name: Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary
description: A tiger reserve in the Ballala Rayana Durga hills built around the Bhadra reservoir backwaters, with gaur, hornbills and jungle lodges on the shore.
how_to_reach: About 20 km from Hosahalli on the Shivamogga–Chikkamagaluru road.
practical_notes: Safari routes and boat rides are set by the forest department; monsoon core-zone closures happen.
entry_fee: Forest entry, guide and safari charges apply; bookings via forest department channels.

name: Hirekolale Lake
description: A high-altitude lake ringed by forest in coffee country, a short drive from Chikkamagaluru and a quiet sunrise spot.
how_to_reach: About 18 km from Chikkamagaluru town via Kemmangundi road.
practical_notes: The approach narrows after rain; no facilities at the lake.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Kudremukh National Park
description: A 1,894 m horse-face shola peak in a national park of stunted forest and streams; the classic Kalasa–Kudremukh ridge trek needs a permit.
how_to_reach: Kalasa village near Balehonnur is the trek base, about 80 km from Chikkamagaluru.
practical_notes: Permits are limited and issued by the forest department; monsoon leeches and zero visibility are real hazards. Drones are banned.
entry_fee: Forest entry, guide and safari charges apply; bookings via forest department channels.

name: Annapoorneshwari Temple, Horanadu
description: A lakeside Annapoorneshwari shrine on the source of the Kumaradhara, famous for its all-day free kitchen serving pilgrims.
how_to_reach: On the Chikkamagaluru–Kalasa–Agumbe road, about 100 km from Chikkamagaluru town.
practical_notes: The annadanam queues move fast; dress code enforced inside.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Hoysaleswara Temple, Halebidu
description: The great Hoysala double-shrine at Halebidu, the Hoysalas' capital Dwarasamudra, its plinths carved wall-to-wall with epics and deities; a component of the UNESCO Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas.
how_to_reach: About 30 km from Hassan town, 16 km from Belur.
practical_notes: Combine with Belur for a single-day Hoysala circuit; site opens through the day.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Shravanabelagola
description: The Jain holy town where the 58-foot monolithic Gommateshwara (Bahubali) stands on Chandranathi hill; the Mahamastakabhisheka anointment at long intervals draws millions.
how_to_reach: About 45 km from Hassan; buses from Bengaluru and Mysuru stop on the highway.
practical_notes: The climb to the statue is 600 open steps; the compound closes at sunset and during major rituals.
entry_fee: Minor entry charges

name: Shettihalli Floating Church
description: An 1864 neo-Gothic mission church beside the Hemavathi backwaters whose lower half disappears under the reservoir each monsoon, giving it the 'floating church' name.
how_to_reach: About 28 km from Hassan via Arasikere road.
practical_notes: Best submerged views are July–December; the site is on private farmland with a public path.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Manjarabad Fort
description: One of India's rare star-shaped forts, built by Tipu Sultan above the Sakleshpur ghat road to guard the Mysuru–Malabar passage.
how_to_reach: On the Sakleshpur–Bisle ghat, about 22 km from Sakleshpur town.
practical_notes: The moat-side paths are eroded; stay on the marked ramparts.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Sakleshpur
description: A coffee, pepper and cardamom hill town on the Mangaluru–Bengaluru mountain railway, the base for Hanuman Guundi, Bisle Falls and Jumbudweep.
how_to_reach: Sakleshpur has a rail halt on the ghats line; road from Hassan is about 60 km.
practical_notes: Train views peak on the clear monsoon-adjacent months; check rail timings before planning.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Kodachadri Hills
description: A 1,343 m peak above Kollur where the Kedar Chulke waterfall drops from the summit rocks; a Shiva pilgrimage hill as well as a trekker's climb.
how_to_reach: About 85 km from Shivamogga via Shiradi ghat and Kollur.
practical_notes: Forest jeeps cover the rough final stretch; monsoon leeches and cloud are common.
entry_fee: Forest entry, guide and safari charges apply; bookings via forest department channels.

name: Agumbe Rainforest
description: The misty 'Camel's Hump' pass on the Shivamogga–Udupi ghats, one of the world's rainiest spots and home to the king cobra research station and Malabar giant squirrels.
how_to_reach: About 100 km from Shivamogga on the Somwarpet–Karkal ghat road.
practical_notes: Leeches after rain; the natural history camp and trek routes are seasonal.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Kundadri Hill
description: A flat-topped granite table hill near Kollur crowned by a small Jain shrine, climbed in a steep half-hour from the forest road.
how_to_reach: About 30 km from Kollur on the Agumbe road.
practical_notes: No shade or water on the rock; early morning is the sensible climb.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Sakrebailu Elephant Camp
description: A forest-department camp on the Linganamakki reservoir backwaters where rescued elephants bathe and graze in open view.
how_to_reach: About 12 km from Sagara town.
practical_notes: Viewing is timed around bathing hours; monsoon levels can cancel the session.
entry_fee: Minor entry charges

name: Gajanur Dam
description: The Kaveri anicut and garden at Gajanur, the river's edge on the way to Sringeri, with backwater views and a riverside temple.
how_to_reach: About 40 km from Shivamogga via Sringeri road.
practical_notes: Garden opens through the day; gates close in heavy spillover.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Keladi (Kikkeri of the Nayakas)
description: The river fortress-capital of the Keladi Nayakas with the Rameshwara temple, a heritage museum of bronzes and copper-plate records of the 16th–18th centuries.
how_to_reach: About 30 km from Shivamogga on the Bangalore highway.
practical_notes: Museum timings are short; the temple pond area is protected.
entry_fee: Museum ticket applies

name: Barkana Falls
description: A segmented fall dropping into the Barkana reservoir forest on the Sakleshpur–Karkal road, strong from June to October.
how_to_reach: About 70 km from Shivamogga via Karkal.
practical_notes: Ghat road after dark is discouraged; no commercial facilities.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Udupi Sri Krishna Math
description: The Madhva tradition's central math, founded in the 13th century, where the Krishna is worshipped through the nine famous 'kitaabi' windows; the paryaya festival rotates among eight mathas.
how_to_reach: Udupi has its own rail station; temple is walkable from the town centre.
practical_notes: Darshan queues peak on purnima and paryaya months; phones not allowed inside.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Malpe Beach
description: Udupi's harbour beach at the mouth of the Sita river, crescent of sand with boat jets for St. Mary's Island and sunset viewpoint on the headland.
how_to_reach: About 6 km from Udupi town; autos and buses run frequently.
practical_notes: Swimming is unsafe at the river mouth; heed posted flags; ferries pause in monsoon.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Kapu (Kaup) Lighthouse Beach
description: A red-and-white banded lighthouse on a sandspit with a ruined fort below and one of the quietest sunsets on the Udupi coast.
how_to_reach: About 15 km from Udupi on the coastal road to Kundapura.
practical_notes: Tower visits depend on coast-guard access; strong undertow at the tip.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Maravanthe Beach
description: The famous stretch where NH-66 runs with the Souparnika river on one side and the Arabian Sea on the other, with the Kodachadri hills closing the view.
how_to_reach: On the coastal highway between Kundapura and Udupi; about 40 km from Udupi.
practical_notes: Crossing to the beach uses local lanes; monsoon seas are dangerous.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Anegudde Kumbharashivana Vinayaka Temple
description: One of the eight Ashta Vinayaka shrines of the Tulu Nadu coast, on a wooded hill above the Sita river, tied to the Parashurama legend.
how_to_reach: About 20 km from Kundapura near Kapu.
practical_notes: Ganesh Chaturthi draws huge crowds; the hill climb has steep steps.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Kollur Mookambika Temple
description: The Shakta seat of Mookambika on the Kollur bank of the Sita river, where a perpetual flame is said to have sunk into the ground, a major learning and pilgrimage centre.
how_to_reach: By road via Byadgi–Kollur ghat, about 90 km from Shivamogga and 60 km from Udupi.
practical_notes: Dress code enforced; festival months (Dec–Jan) are very busy.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Kukke Subramanya Temple
description: One of the seven abodes of Kartikeya, deep in the Kukke forest where the Subrahmanya shrine stands under the Kumara Parvatha peaks.
how_to_reach: About 130 km from Mangaluru or via Sakleshpur rail halt.
practical_notes: Sarpa samskara rituals run by appointment; forest area closes at night.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Panambur Beach
description: Mangaluru's main urban beach, broad and lifeguarded, with a sea-facing park, lighthouse views and the Arabian Sea sunsets the city is known for.
how_to_reach: About 14 km from Mangaluru Junction; city buses run to the beach.
practical_notes: Swim only in patrolled zones; monsoon seas are rough.
entry_fee: Parking and activity charges

name: Tannirbhavi Beach
description: The river-mouth beach across the Netravati from Mangaluru, reached by a short ferry, where the river bends into the sea beneath a casuarina line.
how_to_reach: Ferry from Sultan Bunder; buses from Hampankatta.
practical_notes: Ferry timings set the day; strong currents where river meets sea.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Pilikula Nisargadhama
description: A river-island eco-park at Vittal near Mangaluru with a zoo, aquarium, heritage village, planetarium and boating among coconut groves.
how_to_reach: About 22 km from Mangaluru on the Mangaluru–Moodbidri road.
practical_notes: Rides have separate tickets; closed weekly for maintenance.
entry_fee: Park tickets apply

name: Mangaladevi Temple
description: The shrine of the goddess who gives Mangaluru its name, set on the Murde Hills at the old port, linked to the Gharana of the Saptakanya legend.
how_to_reach: About 3 km from the city centre; autos from Hampankatta.
practical_notes: Steep steps to the hill shrine; theNavaratri bhajans get very crowded.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Kateel Durga Parameshwari Temple
description: The ancient Durga shrine on the Nandini river, one of the Tulu Nadu's most active temples, whose annadanam feeds thousands daily.
how_to_reach: About 55 km from Mangaluru via Moodbidri.
practical_notes: Special poojas fill early; the Aane (elephant) processions draw festival crowds.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Yana Caves
description: Twin black-monolith pinnacles, Mohini Shikara and Bhirameshvara, rising out of the Mandu-Mara forest near Bhatkal; a night-torch trek tradition since colonial times.
how_to_reach: About 95 km from Dandeli via Jatti; the village base is reached by road, then a 9 km forest walk.
practical_notes: Trek is closed in heavy monsoon; torches and water are essential. The rocks are sacred to local communities.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Sathodi Falls
description: A broad tiered fall dropping onto rocks near the Supa backwater forest, popular for a picnic and short dip in the low-flow months.
how_to_reach: About 35 km from Dandeli on the Supa road.
practical_notes: Slippery rocks; no lifeguards; monsoon levels are dangerous.
entry_fee: Minor entry charges

name: Unchalli Falls
description: The Kulas Mara river plunges into a horseshoe gorge at Unchalli; viewpoints and steps are set in reserved forest.
how_to_reach: About 35 km from Dandeli towards Hubballi.
practical_notes: Forest gate timings are short; mist can hide the fall entirely.
entry_fee: Forest entry, guide and safari charges apply; bookings via forest department channels.

name: Karwar Beach
description: The quiet harbour-side beach of Karwar town, where Rabindranath Tagore renamed the sands Purna Chandra; the Calimadam and sea-drive give it a mini-Goa feel.
how_to_reach: Karwar is on the Konkan Railway; beach is walkable from town.
practical_notes: Rocky stretches at both ends; watch the tide before wading.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Mirjan Fort
description: A laterite sea-fort of the 'Queen of Mirjan', its curtain walls enclosing the teak balconies of the palace ruins above the Kalanadi creek.
how_to_reach: About 10 km from Yellapur on the Karwar–Hubballi road.
practical_notes: Windswept ramparts with no shade; combine with Unchalli or Sathodi.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Gokak Falls
description: The Ghataprabha river falls 52 metres through a horseshoe canyon at Gokak, nicknamed the 'Niagara of Karnataka', with an old causeway and a Mahadeva temple opposite.
how_to_reach: About 65 km from Belagavi; Gokak Road station is closer.
practical_notes: Flow peaks Sept–Jan; viewpoints are crowded on holidays.
entry_fee: Entry and parking charges

name: Godachinmalki Falls
description: A 90-metre drop in the remote Kulkarni Wada forest of the Belagavi ghats, reached through a teak and bamboo belt.
how_to_reach: About 70 km from Belagavi via Kherlapur road; last stretch is a forest track.
practical_notes: No facilities; best visited with a local guide Oct–Feb.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Belagavi (Belgaum) Fort
description: A moated fort first raised in the 13th century, rebuilt under the Vijayanagara and Adil Shahi eras, holding Kampli gates, palaces, a Kannada shrine of Adil Shahi art and the Ram Temple where Tilak preached.
how_to_reach: In the old city; auto or walking distance from Belagavi bus stand.
practical_notes: Some inner monuments are locked off-hours; gates open daily.
entry_fee: Entry charges apply

name: Kittur Fort and Palace
description: The fortified palace of the Kittur durbar, remembered for the rani Chennamma's 1824 revolt against the British and its Dussehra court.
how_to_reach: About 25 km from Belagavi via Khanapur road.
practical_notes: The palace is a protected monument; festival days close some areas.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Jamboti Hills
description: A forest border range above the Chandoli valley with Chorla Ghati viewpoint, Mahudabhadra and Vajrapoha waterfalls, and a quiet eco-trek network.
how_to_reach: About 50 km from Belagavi via Saundatti–Khanapur; the road enters reserved forest.
practical_notes: Permits needed near the border belt; monsoon leeches.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Vajrapoha Falls
description: A near-vertical 170-metre drop into a cliff gorge in the Kankumbi forest, one of the state's remotest waterfall treks.
how_to_reach: Reached on foot from Kankumbi in the Jamboti range; 4×4 to the village before that.
practical_notes: The approach is an unmarked forest trail with cliff edges; go only with a local guide.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Aihole Temple Complex
description: The 'cradle of Chalukyan temple architecture', more than a hundred shrines from the 5th–8th centuries scattered through a village landscape, including the Durga, Ladkhan and Meguti temples.
how_to_reach: About 35 km from Badami on the Pattadakal road.
practical_notes: Sites are spread out; a full day combines Badami and Pattadakal.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Banashankari Amma Temple, Badami
description: The Chaulukyan-era Banashankari Amma shrine rebuilt in the 17th century, where a five-day chariot festival with the 'banajashwari' music draws all of Badami.
how_to_reach: At the foot of the Agastya Tanka lake, a short walk from the cave temples.
practical_notes: Photography inside the sanctum is prohibited; festival weeks are extremely crowded.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Mahakuta Group of Temples
description: A cluster of Kadamba-era and later Shiva temples 11 km from Badami on the Aihole road, standing in a sacred tank.
how_to_reach: Taxi from Badami on the Aihole highway.
practical_notes: The compound opens through the day; the tank steps are steep.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Almatti Dam and Garden
description: The Krishna river reservoir dam between Bagalkote and Vijayapura, its light-and-music garden a regular stopover on the Badami–Hampi drive.
how_to_reach: On NH-52, about 60 km from Bagalkote.
practical_notes: Garden opens evenings; the backwater wind is strong after sunset.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Ibrahim Rauza
description: The tomb of Ibrahim Adil Shah II and his queen, the most complete of the Deccan sultans' garden-tombs, often called the Taj Mahal of the Deccan.
how_to_reach: Walkable from the Gol Gumbaz within old Vijayapura.
practical_notes: Monsoon moss makes floors slick; inner chambers close for rain.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Bara Kaman
description: The twelve-arched shell of an intended grand mausoleum for Ali Adil Shah II, left unfinished when the sultan fell at Kolhapur.
how_to_reach: In the same royal quarter as the Rauza.
practical_notes: Open structure with no shade; go early.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Jama Masjid, Vijayapura
description: One of India's largest congregational mosques, its triple-span courtyard and Persian-flowered dome the signature of Adil Shahi builders.
how_to_reach: In the walled city near the fort; walking distance from Gol Gumbaz.
practical_notes: Visits pause around prayer times; modest dress required.
entry_fee: Minor entry charge

name: Upli Buruj
description: A 16th-century watchtower on the eastern skyline, climbed for the view over the Adil Shahi city.
how_to_reach: Shared autos run towards the tower from the fort road.
practical_notes: The steps are narrow and unguarded.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Gagan Mahal
description: The gateway palace of Ali Adil Shah I, its five great arches once framing an inner harem and durbar.
how_to_reach: In the old city, near the Jama Masjid.
practical_notes: Structure is protected but partially open; no signage inside.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Ballari Fort and Hanumanadri
description: A 1.5 km granite fortress hill held by the Vijayanagara, Mughal and Hyderabad powers, its gates and armoury ruins reached by a stepped climb past the Hanumanadri shrine.
how_to_reach: In the city of Ballari, about 60 km from Hospet.
practical_notes: The 800-step climb is exposed; go at dawn with water.
entry_fee: Entry charges apply

name: Daroji Sloth Bear Sanctuary
description: A dry boulder sanctuary south of Ballari, one of the few reliable places to see sloth bears rescued from the region's bear-dance trade.
how_to_reach: About 60 km from Hampi via Hadagalli.
practical_notes: Viewing is by guided vehicle; sightings not guaranteed.
entry_fee: Forest entry, guide and safari charges apply; bookings via forest department channels.

name: Sandur Hills
description: The iron-ore ridge country north of Hospet, its patchwork of mining pits and the little Sitanagaram palace in Sandur town marking a hard industrial landscape.
how_to_reach: About 30 km from Hospet on the Ballari road.
practical_notes: Mining-zone roads are shared with trucks; visit outside shift hours.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Virupaksha Temple, Hampi
description: The living Shiva temple at Hampi whose 50-metre eastern gopuram rises over the Tungabhadra's south bank, continuously worshipped since at least the 7th century.
how_to_reach: In Hampi village itself; walkable from the guesthouse lanes.
practical_notes: Active ritual space; dress code enforced, shoes left at the gate.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Vittala Temple, Hampi
description: The great Vaishnava complex of the Vijayanagara empire's royal quarter, home of the famous monolithic stone chariot and the musical-pillar mandapa.
how_to_reach: About 3 km east of Hampi village; electric vehicle, cycle or auto from the bridge.
practical_notes: The inner sanctum of the chariot courtyard may close; the walk is fully exposed to sun.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Lotus Mahal
description: An elegant Indo-Islamic pavilion in the royal centre, often identified as the queen's council chambers, its lotus-curved domes made of brick and lime.
how_to_reach: In the secure royal-enclosure zone beyond the underground passages.
practical_notes: Combined with the Elephant Stables in one guarded circuit.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Elephant Stables
description: A vaulted royal stable of nine domed chambers with a central riding-elephant courtyard, showing the Sultanate-influenced arch work of the 15th century.
how_to_reach: Beside the Lotus Mahal in the royal core.
practical_notes: Interpretive signage is limited; a guide helps.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Queen's Bath
description: A fortified pleasure-pavilion with an immense lotus-tank hall, its domed arcade a rare survivor of secular Vijayanagara architecture.
how_to_reach: A short walk from the royal core.
practical_notes: The interior is cool and dark; photography allowed outside.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Matanga Hill
description: The highest rise inside Hampi, an easy stepped scramble over boulder fields, taken at sunrise for the valley and Virupakha Ratha view.
how_to_reach: From Hampi bazaar across the river via the bridge or coracle.
practical_notes: Go with torches and water; snakes and heat are real after 10 a.m.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Anegundi Heritage Village
description: The old temple village across the river from Hampi, associated with the Ramayana's Kishkindha, with Rampa falls, Hanuman-moola caves and Vijayanagara-era gateways.
how_to_reach: Reach from Hospet or via Hampi's bridge by local transport.
practical_notes: Sights are spread across rocky terrain; go with a guide or map.
entry_fee: Minor site charges

name: Anjanadri Hill
description: The hill honoured as Hanuman's birthplace near Anegundi, climbed at dawn for a full Hampi–Tungabhadra panorama.
how_to_reach: Base is reached by village road; last climb is stepped rock.
practical_notes: Carry water; the trail is unshaded.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Kuknoor Mahadeva Temple
description: A thousand-year-old Shiva shrine at Kuknoor near the Tungabhadra, its inscriptions recording Vijayanagara-era grants.
how_to_reach: About 10 km from Koppal town.
practical_notes: Temple hours are short midday.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Bahmani Tombs, Ashtur
description: The octagonal domed mausoleums of the Bahmani sultans at Ashtur, their glazed interiors the earliest surviving Deccan royal tombs.
how_to_reach: About 5 km from Bidar fort on the main road.
practical_notes: Sun exposure on the platform is intense; morning visits are best.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Rangin Mahal, Bidar Fort
description: The 'colourful palace' inside Bidar fort, its carved teak screens, mirror-work and painted ceilings the finest surviving Barid Shahi interiors.
how_to_reach: Within the fort complex; local autos from the city.
practical_notes: Fort gates close by late afternoon.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Narasimha Jhira Cave Temple
description: A cave Narasimha shrine with an underground stream running beneath it, reached by a narrow sloping passage.
how_to_reach: At the foot of the Bidar plateau, about 6 km from the fort.
practical_notes: The passage is low and wet; footwear with grip recommended.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Guru Nanak Jhira Sahib
description: The gurudwara at Bidar marking Guru Nanak's long stay, built around a spring (jhira) and holding a langar that feeds visitors all day.
how_to_reach: Near the Narasimha Jhira road; shared autos from the city.
practical_notes: Respect the langar queue etiquette; photography restricted in halls.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Gulbarga (Kalaburagi) Fort
description: A mud-and-stone fort of the Bahmani capital with seven original gates, the Haft Gumbad tombs inside and the 211-foot Chand Minar tower.
how_to_reach: In the old city; auto or walking from the bus stand.
practical_notes: Inner gates lock in the evening.
entry_fee: Entry charges apply

name: Khwaja Bande Nawaz Dargah
description: The 14th-century Chishti shrine of Bandanawaz Gaza, an annual urs gathering that draws devotees across faiths.
how_to_reach: Adjacent to the fort; walkable.
practical_notes: Active Sufi space; dress modestly and follow qawwali timings.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Sharana Basaveshwara Temple
description: An old Lingayat shrine in the heart of Kalaburagi city, built around the samadhi of the 12th-century teacher Sharana Basaveshwara. Its 36-pillared hall, adjacent lake and the annual jatra and car festival make it one of the city's most active places of worship.
how_to_reach: About 2-3 km from Kalaburagi Junction railway station and the KSRTC stand; auto-rickshaws and city buses cover the old city.
practical_notes: Active temple: dress modestly and follow queue directions. The car festival falls around March-April and draws very large crowds. Confirm darshan timings locally.
entry_fee: Free; donations welcome

name: Buddha Vihar, Kalaburagi
description: A modern Buddhist vihara complex with a stupa and Dhamma museum, a calm landmark of the city's Navayana community.
how_to_reach: In the outer city near the ring road.
practical_notes: Museum hours vary; compound closes by evening.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Raichur Fort
description: A granite doab fortress successively held by the Rashtrakutas, Chalukyas, Vijayanagara, Bahmanis, Mughals and Nizams, its walls studded with inscriptions in several scripts.
how_to_reach: In the old city of Raichur, walkable from the station.
practical_notes: Open structure with little shade; early morning is best.
entry_fee: Entry charges apply

name: Ek Minar Ki Masjid
description: The single-minaret mosque of old Raichur, a compact Adil Shahi-era prayer hall built with captured Vijayanagara pillars.
how_to_reach: Beside the fort on the tank road.
practical_notes: Interior access depends on the waqf schedule.
entry_fee: Minor entry charge

name: Aam Talab (Mango Tank)
description: The historic stepped tank and its 15th-century gateway mosque that anchored the old city's water supply.
how_to_reach: In the lane market near the fort.
practical_notes: Crowded bazaar access; watch for scooters.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Chandravalli Caves
description: A bowl valley near Chitradurga whose layered digs reveal megalithic, Chalukyan and Hoysala strata, with rock-cut cells on the rim.
how_to_reach: About 13 km from Chitradurga town.
practical_notes: The path is open ground with no shade; combine with the Jogimatti drive.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Vani Vilasa Sagar
description: One of Mysore state's first big storage reservoirs on the Swarnamukhi, its masonry dam and garden a quiet stopover between Chitradurga and Hosadurga.
how_to_reach: About 40 km from Chitradurga town.
practical_notes: Garden opens through the day; water-level safety signs must be respected.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Jogimatti
description: A hill sanctuary above Chitradurga with cave maths, vultures and a cable-car ride, a monastic retreat for centuries.
how_to_reach: Road or ropeway from the town; jeeps run up in the day.
practical_notes: Ropeway suspends in bad weather; monkeys grab food packs.
entry_fee: Ropeway and entry charges

name: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary
description: Six islands in the Kaveri at Srirangapatna where painted storks, pelicans and mugger crocodiles crowd the banks; the boat glide is the classic way to see them.
how_to_reach: About 4 km from Srirangapatna on the Mysuru road.
practical_notes: Boats run short timed circuits; best in dry months for bird density.
entry_fee: Boat and entry charges

name: Srirangapatna
description: The Kaveri island capital of Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan: the Daria Daulat Bagh summer palace with its battle murals, the Gumbaz graveyard, the Ranganatha temple and the spot where Tipu fell in 1799.
how_to_reach: About 15 km from Mysuru; on the Bangalore–Mysuru highway.
practical_notes: Several monuments share one ticket; check closing day.
entry_fee: Ticketed circuit

name: Krishnaraja Sagar (KRS) Dam
description: The great masonry dam across the Kaveri completed in 1938 under the Mysore diwan, its 1 km stretch of brick a landmark of engineering heritage.
how_to_reach: About 20 km from Mysuru via Srirangapatna.
practical_notes: The top walkway is crowded at weekends; strong winds in monsoon spillover.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Brindavan Gardens
description: The terraced gardens below the KRS dam laid out for the Dasara season, with the famous terrace-mirror and musical fountain illumination at night.
how_to_reach: Beside the dam, about 23 km from Mysuru.
practical_notes: Fountain runs on evenings; some zones close for maintenance.
entry_fee: Garden ticket applies

name: Shivanasamudra Falls
description: The Kaveri splits into the island town of Shivanasamudra and drops in two great faces, Gaganachukki and Bharachukki, beside India's first hydro-electric station (1902).
how_to_reach: About 70 km from Mysuru via Malavalli; Mandya side.
practical_notes: Viewpoints are strongest June–December; steps are wet and crowded at weekends.
entry_fee: Entry charges apply

name: Melukote
description: The hill town of the Vaishnava saint Nammazhwar, its Cheluvanarayana temple and Panchalinga Tirtha tank one of the state's oldest pilgrimage lanes.
how_to_reach: About 45 km from Mysuru off the Srirangapatna road.
practical_notes: The climb is steep; festivals bring huge weekend crowds.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Biligiriranga (BR) Hills
description: The elephant corridor range where the Eastern and Western Ghats meet, with a Ghat road past temple gate, reserve forest and the Hemmadi waterfall.
how_to_reach: About 100 km from Mysuru via Nanjangud.
practical_notes: Night traffic bans in the reserve; leeches after rain.
entry_fee: Forest entry, guide and safari charges apply; bookings via forest department channels.

name: Male Mahadeshwara Hills
description: A 1,500 m forested hill of the Mahadeshwara shrine reached past a monumental gopura gate, with a reserve forest belt around it.
how_to_reach: About 60 km from Mysuru via Nanjangud–Hunsur.
practical_notes: Ghat road is narrow; buses restrict timing.
entry_fee: Forest entry, guide and safari charges apply; bookings via forest department channels.

name: Himavad Gopalaswamy Betta
description: The blue-grassland summit inside the BR range at 1,454 m, cloaked in mist and hosting a Venugopala shrine.
how_to_reach: The forest road leaves the BR hills loop; jeeps with permits only.
practical_notes: Entry controlled by the forest department; fog can erase the view.
entry_fee: Forest entry, guide and safari charges apply; bookings via forest department channels.

name: Devarayanadurga
description: A 1,260 m ridge north of Tumakuru with the Narasimha and Anjaneya hill temples, dawn cloud-river views and a stepped forest climb.
how_to_reach: About 30 km from Tumakuru on the Kunigal road.
practical_notes: Steps are exposed; water at the top is limited.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Siddaganga Math, Tiptur
description: The monastic institution at Tiptur founded by Shivakumara Swamiji, whose car-festival and huge education trusts define the town.
how_to_reach: Tiptur is on the Bangalore–Tumakuru line; math is at the town centre.
practical_notes: The Brahmakalola car festival week (Jan–Feb) is very crowded.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Madhugiri Fort
description: One of the largest monolithic hills in Karnataka, ringed by the ruins of an 18th-century fort whose ramparts run around the bare rock.
how_to_reach: About 30 km from Tumakuru town.
practical_notes: The scramble is exposed granite; go early with grip shoes.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Namada Chilume
description: A forest clearing around a spring that never fails, beneath Devarayanadurga, with a small Kodanda Ramaswamy shrine.
how_to_reach: On the way up to Devarayanadurga; local vehicles from Tumakuru.
practical_notes: Forest gates close by late evening.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Skandagiri Hills
description: A 1,300 m hillock north of Bengaluru with a hilltop temple, the standard pre-dawn trek for a first sunrise view of the plain.
how_to_reach: About 60 km from Bengaluru via Urli Road; village road to the base.
practical_notes: The climb is dark, steep and unlit; groups and guides are the norm.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Bhoga Nandeeshwara Temple
description: The three-shrine Nandi hill-base temple with a spring-fed pool, among the oldest in the region, mentioned in accounts from the 9th century onwards.
how_to_reach: At the foot of Nandi Hills, about 60 km from Bengaluru.
practical_notes: Photography inside restricted; weekends are busy.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Gudibande Fort
description: Tipu Sultan's hill-outpost fort on a 3,200-foot granite dome, its wall circuits a short but steep scramble.
how_to_reach: About 120 km from Bengaluru via Hindupur Road.
practical_notes: No facilities on the hill; carry everything in and out.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Avalabetta
description: One of the highest peaks of the district, a wind-swept grass ridge popular for cross-country treks on the Kalyana range.
how_to_reach: Reached from Nandi–Gauribidanur lanes.
practical_notes: Road access varies with farm seasons; strong winds at the crest.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Ramadevara Betta
description: The leopard reserve hill at Ramanagara, whose boulder-and-scrub slopes give one of the state's easiest serious scrambles and a temple on the saddle.
how_to_reach: Ramanagara is about 50 km southwest of Bengaluru on the Mysuru highway.
practical_notes: Climbing on the rock faces is informal; go with experienced partners.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Janapada Loka
description: The 'world of the people' museum at Kumatadoddi, a hill campus of folk-art galleries, puppets, masks and ritual objects from Karnataka's traditions.
how_to_reach: About 55 km from Bengaluru on the Mysuru highway.
practical_notes: Closed on Mondays; guided sessions need booking.
entry_fee: Entry charges apply

name: Mekedatu
description: The 'tiger's mouth' where the Kaveri squeezes between granite walls at Kanakapura's edge, the legend's goat-leap gorge and a proposed reservoir site.
how_to_reach: About 20 km from Kanakapura; road access from Ramanagara side.
practical_notes: River levels are seasonal and the rocks are sharp; no lifeguards.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Chunchi Falls
description: A seasonal cascade on the Arkavathi off the Bangalore–Mysuru highway, a rocky plunge pool ringed by scrub forest.
how_to_reach: About 40 km from Bengaluru via Sangam/Bannerghatta road.
practical_notes: Flow depends on rain; water is unsafe in the dry months.
entry_fee: Minor entry charges

name: Savandurga
description: Twin monoliths, Doddabetta and Chikkabetta, among Asia's largest single rocks, with temple shrines at the foot and a steep rock climb above.
how_to_reach: About 60 km from Bengaluru via Magadi.
practical_notes: The climb has no railings; start before dawn in summer.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Kolaramma Temple
description: The long-rebuilded Bhoo Devi temple of Kolar, from 10th-century Cholera-era inscriptions through the Vijayanagara additions, one of the region's oldest shrines.
how_to_reach: In Kolar town; buses and autos from Bengaluru via Chikkaballapura.
practical_notes: Daily hours split around midday.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Someshwara Temple, Kolar
description: A Vijayanagara-era Shiva temple in the heart of Kolar town, its granary-style mandapa and inscribed walls showing 15th-century work.
how_to_reach: Walkable from the fort lanes.
practical_notes: Active worship; visit outside puja hours for quiet viewing.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Kotilingeshwara Temple
description: The hill shrine of a hundred-linga tradition on the Kolar plateau, a weekend climb and one of the state's most visited rural temples.
how_to_reach: Approach from Kolar–Mulbagal roads; the climb starts at the village.
practical_notes: Steps are steep and exposed; crowds swell on Mondays.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Antargange
description: The cave-riddled Shatha Shrunga hill of Kolar, its crevices and springs threaded by a barefoot cave-walk route.
how_to_reach: About 70 km from Bengaluru via Devanahalli–Hulimangala Road.
practical_notes: The cave route is dark and tight; head-torches and no big backpacks.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Avani
description: A plateau village in the Kolar district's Ramayana lore, home of the Avani Khad basin, the Sita ammaran guha cave shrine and a summer car-festival.
how_to_reach: About 95 km from Bengaluru via Mulbagal.
practical_notes: Sights are scattered; the water tank is the meeting point.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Chandramouleshwara Temple, Dharwad
description: The 12th-century Keshava temple at the old core of Dharwad, a Kalyani Chalukya–Hoysala bridge-building with a fine open mandapa.
how_to_reach: In the pet (old town) lanes, a 2 km auto from the bus stand.
practical_notes: Worship times restrict quiet photography.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Unkal Lake
description: Dharwad's lake beside the rock outcrop with a Shiva cave shrine, its bund a dawn birding loop and evening walk for two university towns.
how_to_reach: About 4 km from Dharwad centre; Hubballi side by road.
practical_notes: Boating runs seasonally; keep distance from nesting banks.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Nuggikeri Hanuman Temple
description: A hilltop Anjaneya shrine of the Dharwad–Hubballi belt, its well and courtyard built around the legend of a swallowed spear.
how_to_reach: About 15 km from Dharwad; local autos from Alnavar road.
practical_notes: Steep climb; festival days get packed.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Sadhankeri Garden
description: A leafy heritage garden on the Dharwad–Hubballi road, an old estate's park kept up as a green belt for the twin cities.
how_to_reach: On the highway between the cities; auto from either.
practical_notes: Opens in the evening hours mostly.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Trikuteshwara Temple, Gadag
description: The triple-shrine Hindu temple of Gadag, Kalyani Chalukya by plan and Hoysala by detail, its lathe-turned pillars among the finest in the Deccan.
how_to_reach: Gadag is a rail junction on the Hubballi–Bengaluru line.
practical_notes: Temple rituals limit midday entry.
entry_fee: ASI charges apply

name: Lakkundi Temple Complex
description: The temple village of Lakkundi, its Kashivishwanatha, Sangameshwara, Brahma Judi and Manikesha shrines plus an elaborate stepped pushkarani showing the full Chalukya-to-Hoysala transition.
how_to_reach: About 10 km from Gadag town.
practical_notes: Sites are spread across the village; a two-wheeler or guide helps.
entry_fee: ASI charges apply

name: Dambal Temple Village
description: A cluster of 11th–12th-century shrines at Dambal on the Gadag–Bengaluru road, including a Veeranarayana temple and a rare solar icon.
how_to_reach: About 25 km from Gadag towards Bengaluru.
practical_notes: The compound closes by evening.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Veeranarayana Temple, Gadag
description: The great Vishnu temple of Gadag where Chalukyan plan meets Hoysala ornament, an active shrine inside a walled courtyard.
how_to_reach: Walkable from the Trikuteshwara in the old town.
practical_notes: Non-Hindus may be restricted from the inner hall.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Bankapura Peacock Sanctuary
description: A fortified lake sanctuary on the Haveri–Dharwad belt that has run India's peacock breeding programme since 1980, with the 12th-century Doddashankavesha temple beside it.
how_to_reach: About 45 km from Haveri town.
practical_notes: Best during the dawn and dusk display season.
entry_fee: Forest entry applies

name: Ranebennur Blackbuck Sanctuary
description: The open-grass sanctuary that holds one of Karnataka's largest blackbuck herds, with great Indian bustards seen at the margins.
how_to_reach: Ranebennur is on the Haveri–Ranibennur road.
practical_notes: Dawn drive is the rule; sightings depend on season.
entry_fee: Forest entry, guide and safari charges apply; bookings via forest department channels.

name: Siddhesvara Temple, Haveri
description: A mid-12th-century Shiva temple in Haveri town whose star-shaped plan and friezes are a benchmark of the transitional Chalukya-Hoysala style.
how_to_reach: In the temple street of Haveri town centre.
practical_notes: Active worship; visit off-puja hours.
entry_fee: ASI charges apply

name: Galageshwara Temple, Galaganatha
description: A early Chalukyan Shiva temple at Galaganatha near Pattadakal, standing by the Malaprabha river with a distinctive tall shikhara and a large Nandi in its forecourt; commonly visited with the Badami-Pattadakal-Aihole circuit.
how_to_reach: About 20 km from Badami on the Badami-Pattadakal road in Bagalkote district.
practical_notes: Open-air heritage site with limited shade; combine with Pattadakal and Badami in one day.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Santhebennur Step Tank
description: The great stepped pushkarani at Santhebennur, a Hoysala-era water monument of cut-stone terraces, beside a Kalleshwara shrine.
how_to_reach: About 35 km from Davanagere via Mayakonda Road.
practical_notes: Steps are deep and wet in monsoon.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Kalleshwara Temple, Bagali
description: The 11th-century Kalleshwara temple of Bagali, with its perforated screen window and a rare surviving mantapa with an open ramp.
how_to_reach: About 25 km from Davanagere on the Harapanahalli side.
practical_notes: Village access; a local guide finds the compound.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Yadgir Fort
description: The 'fort of the plain' on a rocky rise above Yadgir town, one of the oldest recorded strongholds of the Doab, later held by Vijayanagara and the Nizam.
how_to_reach: In the old town near the bus stand.
practical_notes: Structures are weathered; access is open-air.
entry_fee: Entry charges vary

name: Shahapur Fort
description: A ruined hill fort at Shahapur above the Bhima belt, once a granary of the Deccan sultanates.
how_to_reach: About 25 km from Yadgir.
practical_notes: The trail is unmarked; confirm access locally.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Sannati Buddhist Site
description: One of the largest unexcavated Buddhist complexes in southern India on the Bhima's bank, ringed by a 2,000-year-old brick stupa mound and a later Aihole-style Mahadeva temple.
how_to_reach: About 40 km from Yadgir near the Andhra border.
practical_notes: Village stay is basic; the mound area is protected.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Narayanpur Dam
description: The Tungabhadra reservoir at Narayanpur, a wide backwater on the Yadgir–Koppal line with a small shrine and a causeway drive.
how_to_reach: On the state highway between Koppal and Yadgir.
practical_notes: Winds on the causeway; avoid dusk by the water.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Srikanteshwara Temple, Nanjangud
description: The 'Dakshina Kashi' of the Kabini: a sprawling Hoysala-and-later Shiva complex whose annual Rathotsavam carries a huge chariot through the town.
how_to_reach: About 30 km from Mysuru on the Gundlupet road; Nanjangud has a rail halt.
practical_notes: Temple opens early and closes over midday; car-festival weeks are packed.
entry_fee: Free entry; dress modestly, photography restrictions inside. Timings vary on festival days.

name: Mudgal Fort
description: A hill-top fortress at Mudgal in Lingsugur taluk, held in turn by the Seuna Yadavas, Kakatiyas, Bahmani sultans, Vijayanagara and the Bijapur Adil Shahis, whose Hindu-style masonry and Muslim arched parapets still stand together. The town also preserves Seuna Yadava inscriptions and a pre-1557 Jesuit church.
how_to_reach: About 10 km south-west of Lingsugur in Raichur district, reached by state highway from Raichur or Hubballi; Raichur is the nearest railhead.
practical_notes: The moat, bastions and Fateh Darwaza barbican are open-air ruins with little shade; visit early. Climb only stable masonry.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; ticket rates apply, confirm timings on arrival.

name: Jhari Falls (Dabdabe Falls)
description: A cataract on the slope below Mullayanagiri and Baba Budangiri, where mountain water spreads into a wide, thin white sheet over dark rock. Locally also called Dabdabe or Buttermilk Falls, it is commonly combined with a Mullayanagiri visit.
how_to_reach: About 24 km from Chikkamagaluru town; the last few kilometres are reached by jeep or on foot from the road head. Kadur is the nearest rail station.
practical_notes: Flow depends on rain and melts; rock is wet and slippery and monsoon spray is strong. Wear grip footwear and stay outside the waterline.
entry_fee: Forest entry, guide and safari charges apply; bookings via forest department channels.

name: Kumaraswamy Temple, Krauncha Giri
description: An 8th-10th-century shrine inside the Swamimale hill range about 10 km from Sandur, traditionally honoured as the first abode of Kartikeya (Murugan) in south India. It stands beside the older 7th-8th-century Parvati temple, a notable example of Badami Chalukya middle-phase architecture, and both are protected monuments.
how_to_reach: Approach by road from Sandur town via Karnataka State Highway 40, which passes through the legendary gap in the Krauncha hill; Ballari and Hospet are the nearest railheads.
practical_notes: The hill is forested, cool and known for leopard and venomous-snake habitat; do not stray off the path or visit alone after dusk. The Ghorpade rulers opened the shrine to all communities and lifted the ban on women in 1996.
entry_fee: ASI-protected; confirm access on arrival
address: Krauncha Giri, Sandur taluk, Ballari district

name: Kanakagiri Fort and Temple Town
description: A fortified hill town at Kanakagiri (ancient Suvarnagiri), a former Mauryan provincial seat and later the capital of the Kanakagiri Nayakas, feudatories of Vijayanagara. Its Kanakachalapathi temple complex carries Vijayanagara-era sculpture and portrait figures, with a Jain tirth of Western Ganga origin nearby.
how_to_reach: About 20 km north-west of Gangavathi in Koppal district; the annual Phalguna fair at the temple is the busiest time to reach it.
practical_notes: Fort remains are fragmentary and mixed with the living temple town; the 1586 royal bath of Venkatappa Naik lies on the outskirts. Combine with Hemagudda and Kummata Durga forts if travelling with a vehicle.
entry_fee: Temple free; monument access varies

name: Pavagada Fort
description: A hill fort above Pavagada town in the Tumakuru district's drought plateau, historically part of the Mysore kingdom's border country. The Kote Anjaneya temple at its foothill and the Shani Mahatma temple mark the old town, while the nearby Pavagada Solar Park is now the taluk's best-known sight.
how_to_reach: On the Tumakuru-Hadagalli road, about 100 km from Tumakuru town; Chitradurga is the closer railhead and Bengaluru is roughly 158 km away.
practical_notes: Summit access is restricted in places and the stone is exposed and hot by mid-morning; go early with water. Check local access before the climb.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Kunduvada Lake (Kundavada Kere)
description: A city-edge lake inside Davanagere, maintained as a local recreation and birding spot rather than a tourist attraction, with a bund walk and open green space on the urban fringe.
how_to_reach: Reached from Davanagere town centre by auto or on foot, depending on the entry side used.
practical_notes: A civic amenity: levels, lighting and access vary, and water quality limits swimming. Visit at dawn or dusk for birds; follow local signage.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking or guide charges may apply.

name: Basaveshwara Temple, Basavana Bagewadi
description: A temple town on the Vijayapura-Bengaluru highway, revered by Lingayats as the birthplace of the 12th-century reformer Basavanna. The shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva and Nandi dates to the 11th-century Chalukya period, with a separate Basava Smarak marking the birthplace.
how_to_reach: About 44 km from Vijayapura on NH-13 towards Bagalkot/Bengaluru; Basavana Bagewadi is also a taluka headquarters with bus services from Vijayapura and Bagalkot.
practical_notes: An active pilgrimage town rather than a ticketed monument; the birthplace shrine is managed by the Kudalasangam Development Authority. Visit outside festival days for quieter darshan.
entry_fee: Free; donations welcome
